title: Der gläserne Sarg
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 163. Text from Wikisource (twice proofread against the original). 1857 spelling preserved exactly (daß, gieng, Schloß, Muth, nöthig).
about: KHM 163 sends a wandering tailor into a forest at nightfall, where he witnesses a fight between a bull and a stag and follows the loser underground into a hidden chamber. There he finds a whole enchanted castle shrunk into glass vessels and a noblewoman asleep in a glass coffin, held captive along with her lands by a black magician who murdered her parents and turned her brother into that bull. The poor-tailor-makes-good frame carries an unusually elaborate embedded tale, told in the maiden's own voice once she wakes.

sentences.t: Sage niemand daß ein armer Schneider es nicht weit bringen und nicht zu hohen Ehren gelangen könne, es ist weiter gar nichts nöthig als daß er an die rechte Schmiede kommt und, was die Hauptsache ist, daß es ihm glückt.
sentences.l: Let no one say that a poor tailor cannot get far and cannot rise to high honours; nothing else at all is needful but that he come to the right forge and — what is the main thing — that it turns out lucky for him.
sentences.i: Let no one say that a poor tailor cannot get far and rise to high honours; nothing more is needed than that he come to the right smithy and — what matters most — that fortune favour him.
sentences.n: “Sage niemand daß …” — a verb-first exhortation, “let no one say that …,” with “könne” in the subjunctive of reported speech. “an die rechte Schmiede kommen” is a proverb: to come to the right forge, i.e. apply in the right quarter. “nöthig” (1857) = nötig, needful.

sentences.t: Ein solches artiges und behendes Schneiderbürschchen gieng einmal seiner Wanderschaft nach und kam in einen großen Wald, und weil es den Weg nicht wußte, verirrte es sich.
sentences.l: Such a neat and nimble little tailor-lad once went on his journeyman’s wandering and came into a great forest; and because he did not know the way, he lost himself.
sentences.i: Such a neat and nimble young tailor once set out on his journeyman’s travels and came into a great forest; and as he did not know the way, he lost himself.
sentences.n: “Wanderschaft” is the journeyman’s years of travel from master to master; “seiner Wanderschaft nachgehen” = to pursue one’s wandering. “Schneiderbürschchen” is a double diminutive, a little tailor’s lad — grammatically neuter (hence “es”). “gieng” = ging (1857).

sentences.t: Die Nacht brach ein, und es blieb ihm nichts übrig als in dieser schauerlichen Einsamkeit ein Lager zu suchen.
sentences.l: Night fell, and nothing remained to him but to seek a bed in this eerie solitude.
sentences.i: Night came on, and nothing was left for him but to look for a resting-place in that eerie solitude.
sentences.n: “einbrechen” (of night) = to fall, set in — the separable “ein” closes the clause. “es bleibt ihm nichts übrig als” is a fixed idiom, “nothing remains to him but,” he has no choice but.

sentences.t: Auf dem weichen Mose hätte er freilich ein gutes Bett gefunden, allein die Furcht vor den wilden Thieren ließ ihm da keine Ruhe, und er mußte sich endlich entschließen auf einem Baume zu übernachten.
sentences.l: On the soft moss he would indeed have found a good bed, only the fear of the wild beasts let him have no rest there, and he had at last to resolve to spend the night in a tree.
sentences.i: On the soft moss he would certainly have found a good bed, but his fear of the wild beasts let him have no peace there, and at last he had to resolve to pass the night up a tree.
sentences.n: “Mose” = Moose (dative of Moos, moss) with the old -e ending. “allein” here is the conjunction “only, but,” not the adjective “alone.” “Thieren” (1857) = Tieren, beasts.

sentences.t: Er suchte eine hohe Eiche, stieg bis in den Gipfel hinauf und dankte Gott daß er sein Bügeleisen bei sich trug, weil ihn sonst der Wind, der über die Gipfel der Bäume wehete, weggeführt hätte.
sentences.l: He sought a tall oak, climbed right up into the crown, and thanked God that he carried his flat-iron with him, because otherwise the wind, which blew over the tops of the trees, would have carried him away.
sentences.i: He found a tall oak, climbed right up to the top, and thanked God he had his flat-iron with him, for otherwise the wind blowing over the treetops would have carried him off.
sentences.n: “Bügeleisen” = the tailor’s heavy pressing-iron, here his ballast — a comic touch. “wehete” = wehte, blew; “weggeführt hätte” is the past subjunctive, “would have carried away.” “Gipfel” = treetop, crown.

sentences.t: Nachdem er einige Stunden in der Finsternis, nicht ohne Zittern und Zagen, zugebracht hatte, erblickte er in geringer Entfernung den Schein eines Lichtes; und weil er dachte daß da eine menschliche Wohnung sein möchte, wo er sich besser befinden würde als auf den Ästen eines Baums, so stieg er vorsichtig herab und gieng dem Lichte nach.
sentences.l: After he had passed some hours in the darkness, not without trembling and quailing, he caught sight at a small distance of the gleam of a light; and because he thought that there might be a human dwelling there, where he would fare better than on the branches of a tree, he climbed cautiously down and went after the light.
sentences.i: After he had spent some hours in the dark, not without trembling and dread, he caught sight, a little way off, of the gleam of a light; and thinking there might be some human dwelling there, where he would be better off than on the branches of a tree, he climbed cautiously down and followed the light.
sentences.n: “Zittern und Zagen” is a set alliterative pair, trembling and quailing. “sich befinden” = to fare, be (in a state). “möchte … sein” and “würde” are subjunctives of the tailor’s supposition. “gieng … nach” = ging nach, followed.

sentences.t: Es leitete ihn zu einem kleinen Häuschen, das aus Rohr und Binsen geflochten war.
sentences.l: It led him to a little house that was woven of reed and rushes.
sentences.i: It led him to a little cottage woven of reed and rushes.
sentences.n: “Rohr und Binsen” = reed and rushes; “flechten” (past part. geflochten) = to weave, plait. “Häuschen” is the diminutive of Haus.

sentences.t: Er klopfte muthig an, die Thüre öffnete sich, und bei dem Scheine des herausfallenden Lichtes sah er ein altes eisgraues Männchen, das ein von buntfarbigen Lappen zusammengesetztes Kleid an hatte.
sentences.l: He knocked boldly, the door opened, and by the gleam of the light falling out he saw a little old iron-grey man, who had on a garment put together of many-coloured rags.
sentences.i: He knocked boldly, the door opened, and by the gleam of the light spilling out he saw a little old iron-grey man wearing a garment pieced together from many-coloured rags.
sentences.n: “anklopfen” = to knock (at a door), the “an” at the clause end. “eisgrau” = iron-grey (of hair). “ein … zusammengesetztes Kleid an hatte” — the long attributive phrase sits between article and noun, as German allows; “anhaben” = to have on, wear. “muthig” = mutig; “Thüre” = Türe.

sentences.t: „Wer seid ihr, und was wollt ihr?“ fragte es mit einer schnarrenden Stimme.
sentences.l: “Who are you, and what do you want?” it asked in a rasping voice.
sentences.n: The old man is grammatically “das Männchen,” neuter, so the pronoun is “es,” “it,” though we mean “he.” “ihr” is his brusque plural “you.” “schnarrend” = rasping, grating.

sentences.t: „Ich bin ein armer Schneider,“ antwortete er, „den die Nacht hier in der Wildnis überfallen hat, und bitte euch inständig mich bis Morgen in eurer Hütte aufzunehmen.“
sentences.l: “I am a poor tailor,” he answered, “whom the night has overtaken here in the wilderness, and I beg you urgently to take me in until morning in your hut.”
sentences.i: “I am a poor tailor,” he answered, “caught out by nightfall here in the wilderness, and I earnestly beg you to take me into your hut until morning.”
sentences.n: “überfallen” = to fall upon, overtake (of night). “inständig bitten” = to beg earnestly; “aufnehmen” = to take in, receive. “euch/eurer” are the polite plural “you/your.”

sentences.t: „Geh deiner Wege,“ erwiederte der Alte mit mürrischem Tone, „mit Landstreichern will ich nichts zu schaffen haben; suche dir anderwärts ein Unterkommen.“
sentences.l: “Go your ways,” replied the old man in a surly tone, “with vagabonds I will have nothing to do; seek yourself lodging elsewhere.”
sentences.i: “Be on your way,” replied the old man in a surly tone; “I want nothing to do with vagabonds — find yourself lodging elsewhere.”
sentences.n: “geh deiner Wege” is a set phrase, be off, go your way (genitive “deiner Wege”). “mit … zu schaffen haben” = to have dealings with. “erwiederte” = erwiderte; “anderwärts” = elsewhere.

sentences.t: Nach diesen Worten wollte er wieder in sein Haus schlüpfen, aber der Schneider hielt ihn am Rockzipfel fest und bat so beweglich, daß der Alte, der so böse nicht war als er sich anstellte, endlich erweicht ward und ihn mit in seine Hütte nahm, wo er ihm zu essen gab und dann in einem Winkel ein ganz gutes Nachtlager anwies.
sentences.l: After these words he meant to slip back into his house, but the tailor held him fast by the coat-tail and pleaded so movingly that the old man — who was not so ill-natured as he made himself out to be — was softened at last and took him along into his hut, where he gave him to eat and then assigned him a quite good bed for the night in a corner.
sentences.i: With that he meant to slip back into his house, but the tailor held him fast by the coat-tail and pleaded so movingly that the old man — who was not as bad as he made himself out — softened at last and took him into his hut, where he gave him something to eat and then showed him a very good bed for the night in a corner.
sentences.n: “sich anstellen” = to make a show, pretend (here, to act more ill-tempered than he is). “am Rockzipfel festhalten” = to hold by the coat-tail; “so böse nicht … als” = nicht so böse wie. “erweicht ward” = wurde erweicht, was softened; “anweisen” = to assign, show to.

sentences.t: Der müde Schneider brauchte keines Einwiegens, sondern schlief sanft bis an den Morgen, würde auch noch nicht an das Aufstehen gedacht haben, wenn er nicht von einem lauten Lärm wäre aufgeschreckt worden.
sentences.l: The tired tailor needed no lulling, but slept softly till the morning, and would not yet have thought of getting up, had he not been startled awake by a loud noise.
sentences.i: The tired tailor needed no lulling; he slept soundly till morning, and would not have thought of rising yet, had a loud noise not startled him awake.
sentences.n: “keines Einwiegens brauchen” — “brauchen” with the genitive, to need no lulling-to-sleep (Einwiegen = rocking a child asleep). “wäre … aufgeschreckt worden” is the past subjunctive passive, “had he been startled.”

sentences.t: Ein heftiges Schreien und Brüllen drang durch die dünnen Wände des Hauses.
sentences.l: A violent screaming and bellowing pressed through the thin walls of the house.
sentences.i: A furious screaming and bellowing came through the thin walls of the house.
sentences.n: “dringen durch” = to penetrate, come through. “Schreien” and “Brüllen” are the infinitives used as neuter nouns, the screaming and the bellowing.

sentences.t: Der Schneider, den ein unerwarteter Muth überkam, sprang auf, zog in der Hast seine Kleider an und eilte hinaus.
sentences.l: The tailor, whom an unexpected courage came over, sprang up, in his haste put on his clothes, and hurried out.
sentences.i: The tailor, seized by a sudden courage, sprang up, threw on his clothes in haste, and hurried out.
sentences.n: “überkommen” = to come over, seize (of a feeling). “anziehen” = to put on (clothes), the “an” at the clause end; “aufspringen” = to spring up. “Muth” = Mut.

sentences.t: Da erblickte er nahe bei dem Häuschen einen großen schwarzen Stier und einen schönen Hirsch, die in dem heftigsten Kampfe begriffen waren.
sentences.l: There he caught sight, near the little house, of a great black bull and a fine stag, which were engaged in the fiercest combat.
sentences.i: There, close by the cottage, he saw a great black bull and a fine stag locked in the fiercest combat.
sentences.n: “in einem Kampfe begriffen sein” = to be engaged in a fight (begriffen = caught up in). “Stier” = bull; “Hirsch” = stag — the two enchanted creatures of the tale.

sentences.t: Sie giengen mit so großer Wuth aufeinander los, daß von ihrem Getrampel der Boden erzitterte, und die Luft von ihrem Geschrei erdrönte.
sentences.l: They went at each other with such great fury that the ground trembled from their trampling, and the air resounded from their bellowing.
sentences.i: They went at each other with such fury that the ground shook with their trampling and the air rang with their bellowing.
sentences.n: “losgehen auf” = to go at, attack; “aufeinander los” — the particles pile up at the clause end. “erdröhnen” (erdrönte, 1857) = to resound, ring; “Getrampel” = the trampling.

sentences.t: Es war lange ungewis, welcher von beiden den Sieg davon tragen würde: endlich stieß der Hirsch seinem Gegner das Geweih in den Leib, worauf der Stier mit entsetzlichem Brüllen zur Erde sank, und durch einige Schläge des Hirsches völlig getödtet ward.
sentences.l: It was long uncertain which of the two would carry off the victory: at last the stag drove his antlers into his opponent’s body, whereupon the bull sank to the ground with a dreadful bellow and was wholly killed by a few blows of the stag.
sentences.i: For a long time it was uncertain which of the two would win: at last the stag drove his antlers into his opponent’s body, whereupon the bull sank to the ground with a terrible bellow, and was killed outright by a few blows of the stag.
sentences.n: “den Sieg davontragen” = to carry off the victory. “seinem Gegner das Geweih in den Leib” — the dative “seinem Gegner” is a dative of the person affected, “into his opponent’s body.” “ungewis” = ungewiss; “getödtet ward” = wurde getötet.

sentences.t: Der Schneider, welcher dem Kampfe mit Erstaunen zugesehen hatte, stand noch unbeweglich da, als der Hirsch in vollen Sprüngen auf ihn zu eilte und ihn, ehe er entfliehen konnte, mit seinem großen Geweihe geradezu aufgabelte.
sentences.l: The tailor, who had watched the combat with astonishment, still stood there motionless when the stag, at full leap, rushed toward him and, before he could flee, forked him up outright on its great antlers.
sentences.i: The tailor, who had watched the fight in astonishment, was still standing there motionless when the stag came bounding at him and, before he could escape, tossed him clean up onto its great antlers.
sentences.n: “in vollen Sprüngen” = at full leap, at a bound — “Sprüngen” is the dative plural of the noun der Sprung (leap), NOT the verb it resembles. “auf ihn zu eilen” = to rush toward him; “aufgabeln” = to fork up, pitch up. “Geweihe” = dative of Geweih, antlers, with old -e.

sentences.t: Er konnte sich nicht lange besinnen, denn es gieng schnellen Laufes fort über Stock und Stein, Berg und Thal, Wiese und Wald.
sentences.l: He could not reflect for long, for off it went at a swift run over stock and stone, hill and dale, meadow and wood.
sentences.i: He had no time to collect himself, for off it went at a swift run over stock and stone, hill and dale, meadow and wood.
sentences.n: “sich besinnen” = to reflect, collect one’s thoughts (plain High German here — a shared entry marks the form dialectal, but this is ordinary usage). “schnellen Laufes” is a genitive of manner, “at a swift run.” “über Stock und Stein” = over rough and smooth, a set phrase; “Thal” = Tal.

sentences.t: Er hielt sich mit beiden Händen an die Enden des Geweihes fest und überließ sich seinem Schicksal.
sentences.l: He held himself fast with both hands to the ends of the antlers and gave himself over to his fate.
sentences.i: He held on tight with both hands to the ends of the antlers and gave himself up to his fate.
sentences.n: “sich festhalten an” = to hold fast to (separable “fest”). “sich überlassen” + dative = to give oneself over to.

sentences.t: Es kam ihm aber nicht anders vor als flöge er davon.
sentences.l: But it seemed to him no otherwise than as if he were flying away.
sentences.i: But it seemed to him for all the world as if he were flying away.
sentences.n: “es kommt mir vor” = it seems to me; “nicht anders als” = no otherwise than. “flöge” is the past subjunctive of fliegen after “als,” “as if he were flying.”

sentences.t: Endlich hielt der Hirsch vor einer Felsenwand still und ließ den Schneider sanft herabfallen.
sentences.l: At last the stag stood still before a wall of rock and let the tailor fall gently down.
sentences.i: At last the stag halted before a rock face and let the tailor drop gently down.
sentences.n: “stillhalten” = to hold still, stop; “herabfallen lassen” = to let fall down. “Felsenwand” = a sheer face of rock.

sentences.t: Der Schneider, mehr todt als lebendig, bedurfte längerer Zeit, um wieder zur Besinnung zu kommen.
sentences.l: The tailor, more dead than alive, needed a longer time to come to his senses again.
sentences.i: The tailor, more dead than alive, needed some while to come to his senses again.
sentences.n: “mehr todt als lebendig” = more dead than alive (1857 “todt” = tot). “bedürfen” + genitive (“längerer Zeit”) = to need, require. “zur Besinnung kommen” = to come round, regain one’s senses.

sentences.t: Als er sich einigermaßen erholt hatte, stieß der Hirsch, der neben ihm stehen geblieben war, sein Geweih mit solcher Gewalt gegen eine in dem Felsen befindliche Thüre, daß sie aufsprang.
sentences.l: When he had recovered somewhat, the stag, which had remained standing beside him, struck its antlers with such force against a door set in the rock that it sprang open.
sentences.i: When he had recovered a little, the stag, which had stayed standing beside him, struck its antlers against a door set in the rock with such force that it sprang open.
sentences.n: “einigermaßen” = to some degree, somewhat. “eine in dem Felsen befindliche Thüre” — attributive phrase before the noun, “a door situated in the rock.” “aufspringen” = to spring open.

sentences.t: Feuerflammen schlugen heraus, auf welche ein großer Dampf folgte, der den Hirsch seinen Augen entzog.
sentences.l: Flames of fire beat out, upon which followed a great vapour that withdrew the stag from his eyes.
sentences.i: Flames leapt out, followed by a great cloud of vapour that hid the stag from his sight.
sentences.n: “herausschlagen” (of flames) = to leap, beat out. “den Hirsch seinen Augen entziehen” = to withdraw from one’s eyes, hide from view; “entzog” from entziehen.

sentences.t: Der Schneider wußte nicht was er thun und wohin er sich wenden sollte, um aus dieser Einöde wieder unter Menschen zu gelangen.
sentences.l: The tailor did not know what he should do and where he should turn, to get out of this wilderness again among people.
sentences.i: The tailor did not know what to do or where to turn in order to get out of that wilderness and back among people.
sentences.n: “thun” (1857) = tun. “sich wenden” = to turn; “unter Menschen gelangen” = to reach human company. “Einöde” = wasteland, desolate place.

sentences.t: Indem er also unschlüssig stand, tönte eine Stimme aus dem Felsen, die ihm zurief „tritt ohne Furcht herein, dir soll kein Leid widerfahren.“
sentences.l: While he stood thus irresolute, a voice sounded from the rock, which called to him, “step in without fear; no harm shall befall you.”
sentences.i: As he stood there thus irresolute, a voice sounded out of the rock and called to him, “come in without fear; no harm shall befall you.”
sentences.n: “indem” here is temporal, “while, as.” “zurufen” = to call out to (dative “ihm”). “widerfahren” = to befall, happen to (dative “dir” = you).

sentences.t: Er zauderte zwar, doch, von einer heimlichen Gewalt angetrieben, gehorchte er der Stimme und gelangte durch die eiserne Thür in einen großen geräumigen Saal, dessen Decke, Wände und Boden aus glänzend geschliffenen Quadratsteinen bestanden, auf deren jedem ihm unbekannte Zeichen eingehauen waren.
sentences.l: He did indeed hesitate, yet, driven by a secret power, he obeyed the voice and came through the iron door into a great spacious hall, whose ceiling, walls and floor consisted of brightly polished square-stones, on each of which signs unknown to him were carved.
sentences.i: He hesitated, it is true, yet, driven on by a secret power, he obeyed the voice and passed through the iron door into a great spacious hall whose ceiling, walls and floor were of brightly polished square stones, on each of which signs unknown to him were carved.
sentences.n: “zwar … doch” = “indeed … yet.” “bestehen aus” = to consist of; “geschliffen” = ground, polished. “auf deren jedem” = on each of which (genitive relative); “eingehauen” = hewn, carved in. “Thür” = Tür.

sentences.t: Er betrachtete alles voll Bewunderung und war eben in Begriff wieder hinaus zu gehen, als er abermals die Stimme vernahm, welche ihm sagte „tritt auf den Stein, der in der Mitte des Saales liegt, und dein wartet großes Glück.“
sentences.l: He looked at everything full of wonder and was just on the point of going out again, when he heard the voice once more, which said to him, “step onto the stone that lies in the middle of the hall, and great fortune awaits you.”
sentences.i: He gazed at everything in wonder and was just on the point of going out again when he heard the voice once more, saying to him, “step onto the stone that lies in the middle of the hall, and great fortune awaits you.”
sentences.n: “in Begriff sein zu” = to be on the point of. “abermals” = once again; “vernehmen” = to perceive, hear. “dein wartet großes Glück” — “warten” here takes the genitive “dein,” great fortune awaits you.

sentences.t: Sein Muth war schon so weit gewachsen, daß er dem Befehle Folge leistete.
sentences.l: His courage had already grown so far that he obeyed the command.
sentences.i: His courage had grown so far by now that he obeyed the command.
sentences.n: “Folge leisten” + dative = to comply with, obey (a command). “Muth” = Mut; “dem Befehle” has the old dative -e.

sentences.t: Der Stein begann unter seinen Füßen nachzugeben und sank langsam in die Tiefe hinab.
sentences.l: The stone began to give way under his feet and sank slowly down into the depth.
sentences.i: The stone began to give way under his feet and sank slowly down into the depths.
sentences.n: “nachgeben” = to yield, give way; “hinabsinken” = to sink down, the “hinab” marking motion down and away.

sentences.t: Als er wieder feststand, und der Schneider sich umsah, befand er sich in einem Saale, der an Umfang dem vorigen gleich war.
sentences.l: When it stood firm again, and the tailor looked about him, he found himself in a hall that was equal in extent to the former one.
sentences.i: When it came to rest again and the tailor looked about him, he found himself in a hall equal in size to the one before.
sentences.n: “feststehen” = to stand firm, come to rest. “sich umsehen” = to look around; “an Umfang gleich” = equal in extent; “dem vorigen” = to the previous (hall).

sentences.t: Hier aber gab es mehr zu betrachten und zu bewundern.
sentences.l: Here, however, there was more to look at and to wonder at.
sentences.i: Here, though, there was more to look at and to marvel at.
sentences.n: “es gibt … zu” + infinitive = there is (something) to be done. “betrachten” = to observe, contemplate; “bewundern” = to admire, wonder at.

sentences.t: In die Wände waren Vertiefungen eingehauen, in welchen Gefäße von durchsichtigem Glase standen, die mit farbigem Spiritus oder mit einem bläulichen Rauche angefüllt waren.
sentences.l: Into the walls hollows were carved, in which stood vessels of transparent glass, filled with coloured spirit or with a bluish smoke.
sentences.i: Recesses were cut into the walls, in which stood vessels of clear glass filled with coloured spirit or with a bluish smoke.
sentences.n: “von durchsichtigem Glase” = of transparent glass — “Glase” is the dative of Glas with an old -e, ordinary High German here (though a shared entry marks the form dialectal). “Spiritus” = spirit (alcohol); “Rauche” = dative of Rauch, smoke; “angefüllt” = filled up.

sentences.t: Auf dem Boden des Saales standen, einander gegenüber, zwei große gläserne Kasten, die sogleich seine Neugierde reizten.
sentences.l: On the floor of the hall stood, opposite each other, two great glass cases, which at once excited his curiosity.
sentences.i: On the floor of the hall, facing each other, stood two great glass cases, which at once aroused his curiosity.
sentences.n: “einander gegenüber” = opposite one another. “gläserne Kasten” = glass cases, chests; “die Neugierde reizen” = to excite curiosity.

sentences.t: Indem er zu dem einen trat, erblickte er darin ein schönes Gebäude, einem Schlosse ähnlich, von Wirthschaftsgebäuden, Ställen und Scheuern und einer Menge anderer artigen Sachen umgeben.
sentences.l: As he stepped up to the one, he caught sight within it of a fine building, like a castle, surrounded by farm-buildings, stables and barns and a host of other pretty things.
sentences.i: As he stepped up to the one, he saw within it a fine building, like a castle, surrounded by outbuildings, stables and barns and a host of other charming things.
sentences.n: “indem” temporal again, “as.” “einem Schlosse ähnlich” — “ähnlich” takes the dative, “like a castle.” “Wirthschaftsgebäude” (1857) = Wirtschaftsgebäude, farm outbuildings; “Scheuern” = barns; “artig” here = pretty, dainty.

sentences.t: Alles war klein, aber überaus sorgfältig und zierlich gearbeitet, und schien von einer kunstreichen Hand mit der höchsten Genauigkeit ausgeschnitzt zu sein.
sentences.l: Everything was small, but exceedingly carefully and daintily wrought, and seemed to have been carved out by an artful hand with the highest exactness.
sentences.i: Everything was small, but exceedingly careful and delicate in its workmanship, and seemed to have been carved by a skilful hand with the utmost precision.
sentences.n: “überaus” = exceedingly. “von einer kunstreichen Hand … ausgeschnitzt” = carved by an artful hand (passive with “von”); “ausschnitzen” = to carve out.

sentences.t: Er würde seine Augen von der Betrachtung dieser Seltenheiten noch nicht abgewendet haben, wenn sich nicht die Stimme abermals hätte hören lassen.
sentences.l: He would not yet have turned his eyes from the contemplation of these rarities, had not the voice let itself be heard again.
sentences.i: He would not yet have turned his eyes from these rare sights, had the voice not made itself heard again.
sentences.n: A contrary-to-fact conditional: “würde … abgewendet haben … wenn … hätte hören lassen.” “sich hören lassen” = to make oneself heard. “Seltenheiten” = rarities, curiosities.

sentences.t: Sie forderte ihn auf sich umzukehren und den gegenüberstehenden Glaskasten zu beschauen.
sentences.l: It called on him to turn round and to view the glass case standing opposite.
sentences.i: It bade him turn round and look at the glass case opposite.
sentences.n: “auffordern” = to call on, bid (separable “auf”). “sich umkehren” = to turn round; “beschauen” = to look at, examine. “Sie” refers back to “die Stimme,” the voice — feminine, hence “it.”

sentences.t: Wie stieg seine Verwunderung als er darin ein Mädchen von größter Schönheit erblickte.
sentences.l: How his amazement rose when he caught sight within it of a maiden of the greatest beauty.
sentences.i: How his amazement grew when he saw within it a maiden of the greatest beauty.
sentences.n: “wie stieg seine Verwunderung” — an exclamatory “how his wonder rose,” though printed with a full stop. “von größter Schönheit” = of the greatest beauty.

sentences.t: Es lag wie im Schlafe, und war in lange blonde Haare wie in einen kostbaren Mantel eingehüllt.
sentences.l: It lay as if in sleep, and was wrapped in long fair hair as in a costly mantle.
sentences.i: She lay as if asleep, wrapped in long fair hair as in a costly mantle.
sentences.n: “Mädchen” is neuter, so “es” = “it,” though we mean “she.” “im Schlafe” has the old dative -e; “einhüllen in” = to wrap in. “blond” = fair.

sentences.t: Die Augen waren fest geschlossen, doch die lebhafte Gesichtsfarbe und ein Band, das der Athem hin und her bewegte, ließen keinen Zweifel an ihrem Leben.
sentences.l: The eyes were firmly closed, yet the lively colour of the face and a ribbon that the breath moved to and fro left no doubt of her life.
sentences.i: Her eyes were tightly shut, yet the fresh colour of her face and a ribbon stirred to and fro by her breath left no doubt that she lived.
sentences.n: “Gesichtsfarbe” = complexion, colour of the face. “Athem” (1857) = Atem, breath; “hin und her” = to and fro. “keinen Zweifel an … lassen” = to leave no doubt about.

sentences.t: Der Schneider betrachtete die Schöne mit klopfendem Herzen, als sie plötzlich die Augen aufschlug und bei seinem Anblick in freudigem Schrecken zusammenfuhr.
sentences.l: The tailor regarded the fair one with beating heart, when she suddenly opened her eyes and, at the sight of him, started up in joyful fright.
sentences.i: The tailor gazed at the fair one with beating heart, when suddenly she opened her eyes and, at the sight of him, started in joyful alarm.
sentences.n: “die Schöne” = the beautiful one (adjective as noun). “die Augen aufschlagen” = to open one’s eyes; “zusammenfahren” = to start, give a jolt. “freudiger Schrecken” = a glad shock, joyful fright.

sentences.t: „Gerechter Himmel,“ rief sie, „meine Befreiung naht!
sentences.l: “Righteous Heaven,” she cried, “my deliverance draws near!
sentences.i: “Just Heaven,” she cried, “my deliverance is at hand!
sentences.n: “gerechter Himmel” is an exclamation, “righteous, just Heaven!” “nahen” = to draw near, approach. Her speech runs on into the next sentence.

sentences.t: geschwind, geschwind, hilf mir aus meinem Gefängnis: wenn du den Riegel an diesem gläsernen Sarg wegschiebst, so bin ich erlöst.“
sentences.l: quick, quick, help me out of my prison: if you push away the bolt on this glass coffin, then I am released.”
sentences.i: quick, quick, help me out of my prison — if you slide back the bolt of this glass coffin, then I am set free.”
sentences.n: “geschwind” = quick(ly). “wegschieben” = to push away, slide back (separable “weg”). “gläserner Sarg” = glass coffin — the title image; “erlöst” = redeemed, released. “du” is “you.”

sentences.t: Der Schneider gehorchte ohne Zaudern, alsbald hob sie den Glasdeckel in die Höhe, stieg heraus und eilte in die Ecke des Saals, wo sie sich in einen weiten Mantel verhüllte.
sentences.l: The tailor obeyed without hesitation; at once she raised the glass lid up on high, climbed out and hurried into the corner of the hall, where she wrapped herself in a wide mantle.
sentences.i: The tailor obeyed without hesitating; at once she raised the glass lid, climbed out, and hurried to the corner of the hall, where she wrapped herself in a wide mantle.
sentences.n: “ohne Zaudern” = without hesitation. “in die Höhe heben” = to raise up; “alsbald” = at once, forthwith; “sich verhüllen in” = to wrap oneself in.

sentences.t: Dann setzte sie sich auf einen Stein nieder, hieß den jungen Mann heran gehen, und nachdem sie einen freundlichen Kuß auf seinen Mund gedrückt hatte, sprach sie „mein lang ersehnter Befreier, der gütige Himmel hat mich zu dir geführt und meinen Leiden ein Ziel gesetzt.
sentences.l: Then she sat herself down on a stone, bade the young man come near, and after she had pressed a friendly kiss upon his mouth, she spoke, “my long-yearned-for deliverer, kind Heaven has led me to you and set an end to my sufferings.
sentences.i: Then she sat down on a stone, bade the young man come near, and after she had pressed a warm kiss on his lips, she said, “my long-awaited deliverer, kind Heaven has led me to you and set a term to my sufferings.
sentences.n: “sich niedersetzen” = to sit down (separable “nieder”). “heißen” + infinitive = to bid (someone do); “lang ersehnt” = long yearned-for. “einer Sache ein Ziel setzen” = to set a limit, an end to something; “dir” = you.

sentences.t: An demselben Tage, wo sie endigen, soll dein Glück beginnen.
sentences.l: On the very day where they end, your fortune shall begin.
sentences.i: On the very day they end, your good fortune shall begin.
sentences.n: “an demselben Tage” = on the same, the very day (old dative -e); “wo” used for “an dem,” “on which.” “endigen” = to end, cease. “dein” = your.

sentences.t: Du bist der vom Himmel bestimmte Gemahl, und sollst, von mir geliebt und mit allen irdischen Gütern überhäuft, in ungestörter Freud dein Leben zubringen.
sentences.l: You are the husband appointed by Heaven, and shall, loved by me and heaped with all earthly goods, pass your life in undisturbed joy.
sentences.i: You are the husband ordained by Heaven, and shall, beloved by me and heaped with every earthly good, pass your life in untroubled joy.
sentences.n: “der vom Himmel bestimmte Gemahl” = the spouse appointed by Heaven (attributive phrase before the noun). “überhäuft mit” = heaped with; “ungestörte Freud(e)” = undisturbed joy; “zubringen” = to spend, pass (time). “Du/dein” = you/your.

sentences.t: Sitz nieder und höre die Erzählung meines Schicksals.
sentences.l: Sit down and hear the tale of my fate.
sentences.i: Sit down and hear the story of my fate.
sentences.n: “sitz nieder” = sit down (imperative, separable “nieder”). “Erzählung” = telling, narrative; “Schicksal” = fate, destiny.

sentences.t: „Ich bin die Tochter eines reichen Grafen.
sentences.l: “I am the daughter of a rich count.
sentences.n: “eines reichen Grafen” is genitive, “of a rich count.” The maiden begins her story; the opening quotation mark runs on through the whole block.

sentences.t: Meine Eltern starben als ich noch in zarter Jugend war und empfahlen mich in ihren letzten Willen meinem ältern Bruder, bei dem ich auferzogen wurde.
sentences.l: My parents died when I was still in tender youth, and commended me in their last will to my elder brother, with whom I was brought up.
sentences.i: My parents died while I was still in tender youth, and in their last will commended me to my elder brother, in whose house I was brought up.
sentences.n: “in zarter Jugend” = in tender, early youth. “empfehlen” here = to commend, entrust; “letzter Wille” = last will, testament. “auferzogen” = aufgezogen, brought up, reared; “ältern” = älteren.

sentences.t: Wir liebten uns so zärtlich und waren so übereinstimmend in unserer Denkungsart und unsern Neigungen, daß wir beide den Entschluß faßten uns niemals zu verheirathen, sondern bis an das Ende unseres Lebens beisammen zu bleiben.
sentences.l: We loved each other so tenderly and were so much in agreement in our way of thinking and our inclinations that we both formed the resolve never to marry, but to stay together until the end of our life.
sentences.i: We loved each other so tenderly and were so alike in our way of thinking and our inclinations that we both resolved never to marry, but to remain together to the end of our lives.
sentences.n: “Denkungsart” = cast of mind, way of thinking; “Neigungen” = inclinations, leanings. “einen Entschluß fassen” = to form a resolve, resolve; “sich verheirathen” (1857) = sich verheiraten, to marry.

sentences.t: In unserm Hause war an Gesellschaft nie Mangel: Nachbarn und Freunde besuchten uns häufig, und wir übten gegen alle die Gastfreundschaft in vollem Maße.
sentences.l: In our house there was never any lack of company: neighbours and friends visited us often, and we practised hospitality toward all in full measure.
sentences.i: In our house there was never any want of company: neighbours and friends visited us often, and we showed hospitality to all in full measure.
sentences.n: “an etwas Mangel sein” = to be short of, lack something (here “an Gesellschaft,” of company). “Gastfreundschaft üben” = to practise, show hospitality; “in vollem Maße” = in full measure.

sentences.t: So geschah es auch eines Abends, daß ein Fremder in unser Schloß geritten kam und, unter dem Vorgeben den nächsten Ort nicht mehr erreichen zu können, um ein Nachtlager bat.
sentences.l: So it happened too one evening that a stranger came riding into our castle and, under the pretence of not being able to reach the nearest place any more, asked for a night’s lodging.
sentences.i: And so it happened one evening that a stranger came riding into our castle and, on the pretext that he could no longer reach the nearest town, asked for a night’s lodging.
sentences.n: “eines Abends” is a genitive of time, “one evening.” “geritten kam” = came riding (kommen + past participle of manner). “unter dem Vorgeben” = under the pretence; “um … bitten” = to ask for.

sentences.t: Wir gewährten seine Bitte mit zuvorkommender Höflichkeit, und er unterhielt uns während des Abendessens mit seinem Gespräche und eingemischten Erzählungen auf das anmuthigste.
sentences.l: We granted his request with obliging courtesy, and during supper he entertained us with his conversation and interspersed tales in the most charming way.
sentences.i: We granted his request with ready courtesy, and all through supper he entertained us most charmingly with his talk and the tales he wove into it.
sentences.n: “gewähren” = to grant; “zuvorkommend” = obliging, attentive. “auf das anmuthigste” = in the most charming manner (a superlative adverb; “anmuthig” = anmutig). “eingemischt” = mixed in, interspersed.

sentences.t: Mein Bruder hatte ein so großes Wohlgefallen an ihm, daß er ihn bat ein paar Tage bei uns zu verweilen, wozu er nach einigem Weigern einwilligte.
sentences.l: My brother had so great a liking for him that he asked him to tarry a few days with us, to which, after some refusing, he consented.
sentences.i: My brother took such a liking to him that he begged him to stay a few days with us, to which, after some demur, he agreed.
sentences.n: “Wohlgefallen an … haben” = to take pleasure, liking in. “verweilen” = to tarry, stay; “nach einigem Weigern” = after some reluctance; “einwilligen in” (wozu = in was) = to consent to.

sentences.t: Wir standen erst spät in der Nacht vom Tische auf, dem Fremden wurde ein Zimmer angewiesen, und ich eilte, ermüdet wie ich war, meine Glieder in die weichen Federn zu senken.
sentences.l: We rose from the table only late in the night; the stranger was shown a room, and I hastened, tired as I was, to sink my limbs into the soft feathers.
sentences.i: It was late in the night before we rose from the table; the stranger was shown to a room, and I hurried, tired as I was, to sink my limbs into the soft featherbed.
sentences.n: “aufstehen vom Tische” = to rise from the table (old dative -e). “anweisen” = to assign, show to; “die Federn” = the feathers, i.e. the featherbed. “ermüdet wie ich war” = tired as I was.

sentences.t: Kaum war ich ein wenig eingeschlummert, so weckten mich die Töne einer zarten und lieblichen Musik.
sentences.l: Scarcely had I dozed off a little when the tones of a tender and lovely music woke me.
sentences.i: I had scarcely dozed off a little when the strains of a soft and lovely music woke me.
sentences.n: “kaum … so” = scarcely … when; the verb-first “war ich” carries the “hardly” sense. “einschlummern” = to doze off; “Töne” = tones, strains.

sentences.t: Da ich nicht begreifen konnte woher sie kamen, so wollte ich mein im Nebenzimmer schlafendes Kammermädchen rufen, allein zu meinem Erstaunen fand ich daß mir, als lastete ein Alp auf meiner Brust, von einer unbekannten Gewalt die Sprache benommen und ich unvermögend war den geringsten Laut von mir zu geben.
sentences.l: Since I could not grasp where they came from, I wanted to call my chambermaid sleeping in the next room; only, to my astonishment, I found that — as if a nightmare lay on my breast — the speech had been taken from me by an unknown power, and I was incapable of uttering the least sound.
sentences.i: As I could not tell where it came from, I meant to call my chambermaid, who slept in the next room; but to my astonishment I found that — as though a nightmare weighed on my breast — some unknown power had robbed me of speech, and I was unable to utter the least sound.
sentences.n: “da” here = since, because. “mein im Nebenzimmer schlafendes Kammermädchen” — attributive phrase before the noun, “my chambermaid sleeping in the next room.” “Alp” = the nightmare-demon thought to press on the sleeper; “die Sprache benehmen” = to take away speech; “unvermögend” = unable; “von sich geben” = to utter.

sentences.t: Indem sah ich bei dem Schein der Nachtlampe den Fremden in mein durch zwei Thüren fest verschlossenes Zimmer eintreten.
sentences.l: Meanwhile I saw, by the gleam of the night-lamp, the stranger step into my room, which was firmly locked by two doors.
sentences.i: Just then I saw, by the light of the night-lamp, the stranger enter my room, which was securely shut behind two doors.
sentences.n: “indem” here = meanwhile, just then. “durch zwei Thüren fest verschlossen” — attributive phrase before “Zimmer,” “firmly closed by two doors.” “eintreten” = to step in, enter; “Thüren” = Türen.

sentences.t: Er näherte sich mir und sagte daß er durch Zauberkräfte, die ihm zu Gebote ständen, die liebliche Musik habe ertönen lassen um mich aufzuwecken, und dringe jetzt selbst durch alle Schlösser in der Absicht, mir Herz und Hand anzubieten.
sentences.l: He drew near to me and said that by magic powers which stood at his command he had made the lovely music sound in order to wake me, and was now pressing through all the locks himself with the intention of offering me heart and hand.
sentences.i: He drew near me and said that by the magic powers at his command he had made the lovely music sound in order to wake me, and was now forcing his way through every lock himself, meaning to offer me his heart and hand.
sentences.n: “sich nähern” + dative = to approach. “zu Gebote stehen” = to be at one’s command; “ständen,” “habe … lassen” and “dringe” are subjunctives of reported speech. “ertönen lassen” = to make sound; “Herz und Hand anbieten” = to offer heart and hand (in marriage).

sentences.t: Mein Widerwille aber gegen seine Zauberkünste war so groß, daß ich ihn keiner Antwort würdigte.
sentences.l: But my repugnance against his magic arts was so great that I did not deign him any answer.
sentences.i: But my loathing of his magic arts was so great that I did not deign to give him any answer.
sentences.n: “Widerwille gegen” = repugnance, aversion to. “jemanden keiner Antwort würdigen” = not to deign someone an answer (“würdigen” + genitive of the thing granted).

sentences.t: Er blieb eine Zeit lang unbeweglich stehen, wahrscheinlich in der Absicht einen günstigen Entschluß zu erwarten, als ich aber fortfuhr zu schweigen, erklärte er zornig daß er sich rächen und Mittel finden werde meinen Hochmuth zu bestrafen, worauf er das Zimmer wieder verließ.
sentences.l: He remained standing motionless for a while, probably with the intention of awaiting a favourable decision; but when I went on keeping silent, he declared angrily that he would take revenge and find means to punish my haughtiness, whereupon he left the room again.
sentences.i: He stood motionless for a while, probably meaning to wait for a favourable answer; but when I went on keeping silent, he declared angrily that he would take his revenge and find means to punish my pride, and with that he left the room again.
sentences.n: “eine Zeit lang” = for a while. “fortfahren zu” = to go on (doing); “sich rächen” = to take revenge; “Hochmuth” (1857) = Hochmut, haughtiness, pride. “werde … finden” is future subjunctive of reported speech.

sentences.t: Ich brachte die Nacht in höchster Unruhe zu und schlummerte erst gegen Morgen ein.
sentences.l: I passed the night in the utmost unrest and only dozed off towards morning.
sentences.i: I passed the night in the greatest disquiet and only fell asleep towards morning.
sentences.n: “zubringen” = to spend, pass (time). “erst gegen Morgen” = only towards morning; “einschlummern” = to doze off.

sentences.t: Als ich erwacht war, eilte ich zu meinem Bruder, um ihn von dem was vorgefallen war, zu benachrichtigen, allein ich fand ihn nicht auf seinem Zimmer, und der Bediente sagte mir daß er bei anbrechendem Tage mit dem Fremden auf die Jagd geritten sei.
sentences.l: When I had woken, I hurried to my brother to inform him of what had occurred; only, I did not find him in his room, and the servant told me that he had ridden out hunting with the stranger at daybreak.
sentences.i: When I woke, I hurried to my brother to tell him what had happened; but I did not find him in his room, and the servant told me that he had ridden out hunting with the stranger at daybreak.
sentences.n: “benachrichtigen von” = to inform of. “vorfallen” = to occur, happen; “bei anbrechendem Tage” = at breaking day, daybreak; “auf die Jagd reiten” = to ride out to the hunt. “geritten sei” is subjunctive of reported speech.

sentences.t: Mir ahnete gleich nichts gutes.
sentences.l: At once I had a foreboding of no good.
sentences.i: At once I had a foreboding of ill.
sentences.n: “mir ahnet(e) etwas” is impersonal with a dative: “I have a foreboding,” literally “to me something bodes.” “nichts gutes” = nichts Gutes, nothing good.

sentences.t: Ich kleidete mich schnell an, ließ meinen Leibzelter satteln und ritt, nur von einem Diener begleitet, in vollem Jagen nach dem Walde.
sentences.l: I dressed myself quickly, had my palfrey saddled and rode, accompanied only by a servant, at full gallop towards the wood.
sentences.i: I dressed quickly, had my palfrey saddled, and rode, with only a servant to attend me, at full gallop towards the wood.
sentences.n: “sich ankleiden” = to dress (separable “an”). “Leibzelter” = one’s own riding palfrey (Zelter, an ambling horse); “in vollem Jagen” = at full chase, gallop.

sentences.t: Der Diener stürzte mit dem Pferde und konnte mir, da das Pferd den Fuß gebrochen hatte, nicht folgen.
sentences.l: The servant fell with his horse and, since the horse had broken its foot, could not follow me.
sentences.i: The servant fell with his horse and, as the horse had broken its leg, could not follow me.
sentences.n: “stürzen” = to fall, take a tumble. “da” = since, because; “mir folgen” = to follow me (dative). “Fuß” of a horse = leg, foot.

sentences.t: Ich setzte, ohne mich aufzuhalten, meinen Weg fort, und in wenigen Minuten sah ich den Fremden mit einem schönen Hirsch, den er an der Linie führte, auf mich zukommen.
sentences.l: I set my way onward, without stopping, and in a few minutes I saw the stranger coming towards me with a fine stag that he led on a line.
sentences.i: I went on my way without stopping, and in a few minutes I saw the stranger coming towards me with a fine stag that he led on a leash.
sentences.n: “seinen Weg fortsetzen” = to continue on one’s way; “sich aufhalten” = to stop, tarry. “an der Linie führen” = to lead on a line, leash; “auf mich zukommen” = to come towards me.

sentences.t: Ich fragte ihn wo er meinen Bruder gelassen habe und wie er zu diesem Hirsche gelangt sei, aus dessen großen Augen ich Thränen fließen sah.
sentences.l: I asked him where he had left my brother and how he had come by this stag, from whose great eyes I saw tears flowing.
sentences.n: “gelassen habe” and “gelangt sei” are subjunctives of the reported question. “zu etwas gelangen” = to come by, obtain; “aus dessen … Augen” = from whose eyes (genitive relative). “Thränen” (1857) = Tränen. (Here the literal already reads as natural English, so no separate idiomatic line.)

sentences.t: Anstatt mir zu antworten fieng er an laut aufzulachen.
sentences.l: Instead of answering me, he began to laugh out loud.
sentences.i: Instead of answering me, he burst out laughing.
sentences.n: “anstatt … zu” = instead of (doing). “anfangen zu” = to begin to (separable “an”); “fieng” = fing (1857); “auflachen” = to laugh out.

sentences.t: Ich gerieth darüber in höchsten Zorn, zog eine Pistole und drückte sie gegen das Ungeheuer ab, aber die Kugel prallte von seiner Brust zurück und fuhr in den Kopf meines Pferdes.
sentences.l: I fell into the highest rage at this, drew a pistol and fired it at the monster, but the ball rebounded from its breast and drove into the head of my horse.
sentences.i: At this I flew into a rage, drew a pistol and fired it at the monster, but the ball rebounded from its breast and struck into my horse’s head.
sentences.n: “in Zorn gerathen” (1857 gerieth) = to fall into a rage. “abdrücken” = to fire (a gun); “abprallen von” = to rebound from; “Kugel” = ball, bullet.

sentences.t: Ich stürzte zur Erde, und der Fremde murmelte einige Worte, die mir das Bewußtsein raubten.
sentences.l: I fell to the earth, and the stranger murmured a few words that robbed me of consciousness.
sentences.i: I fell to the ground, and the stranger murmured a few words that robbed me of my senses.
sentences.n: “zur Erde stürzen” = to fall to the ground. “jemandem das Bewußtsein rauben” = to rob of consciousness (dative “mir”).

sentences.t: Als ich wieder zur Besinnung kam fand ich mich in dieser unterirdischen Gruft in einem gläsernen Sarge.
sentences.l: When I came to my senses again, I found myself in this underground vault in a glass coffin.
sentences.i: When I came to my senses again, I found myself in this underground vault, in a glass coffin.
sentences.n: “zur Besinnung kommen” = to regain one’s senses. “Gruft” = vault, crypt; “in einem gläsernen Sarge” (old dative -e) = in a glass coffin — the title image again.

sentences.t: Der Schwarzkünstler erschien nochmals, sagte daß er meinen Bruder in einen Hirsch verwandelt, mein Schloß, mit allem Zubehör, verkleinert, in den andern Glaskasten eingeschlossen, und meine in Rauch verwandelten Leute in Glasflaschen gebannt hätte.
sentences.l: The black-artist appeared once more, said that he had changed my brother into a stag, shrunk my castle with all its appurtenances and shut it in the other glass case, and banished my people, turned into smoke, into glass bottles.
sentences.i: The sorcerer appeared once more and said that he had turned my brother into a stag, shrunk my castle with all its outbuildings and shut it in the other glass case, and, having turned my people into smoke, banished them into glass bottles.
sentences.n: “Schwarzkünstler” = worker of the black art, sorcerer. “verwandeln in” = to transform into; “verkleinern” = to make smaller; “bannen” = to bind by spell, banish. “hätte … verwandelt … eingeschlossen … gebannt” — subjunctive of reported speech throughout.

sentences.t: Wolle ich mich jetzt seinem Wunsche fügen, so sei ihm ein leichtes, alles wieder in den vorigen Stand zu setzen: er brauche nur die Gefäße zu öffnen, so werde alles wieder in die natürliche Gestalt zurückkehren.
sentences.l: If I would now yield to his wish, it would be an easy thing for him to set everything back into its former state: he need only open the vessels, and everything would return again into its natural shape.
sentences.i: If I would now yield to his wish, it would be easy for him to restore everything to its former state: he need only open the vessels, and all would return to its natural shape.
sentences.n: The whole sentence is the sorcerer’s offer in reported speech — hence the subjunctives “wolle, sei, brauche, werde.” “sich fügen” + dative = to submit to; “in den vorigen Stand setzen” = to put back into the former state; “es ist mir ein leichtes” = it is an easy thing for me.

sentences.t: Ich antwortete ihm so wenig als das erste Mal.
sentences.l: I answered him as little as the first time.
sentences.i: I answered him no more than the first time.
sentences.n: “so wenig als” = so wenig wie, as little as. She keeps the same defiant silence.

sentences.t: Er verschwand und ließ mich in meinem Gefängnisse liegen, in welchem mich ein tiefer Schlaf befiel.
sentences.l: He vanished and let me lie in my prison, in which a deep sleep fell upon me.
sentences.i: He vanished and left me lying in my prison, where a deep sleep came over me.
sentences.n: “liegen lassen” = to leave lying. “Gefängnisse” has the old dative -e; “befallen” = to befall, come over (of sleep); “befiel” from befallen.

sentences.t: Unter den Bildern, welche an meiner Seele vorübergiengen, war auch das tröstliche, daß ein junger Mann kam und mich befreite, und als ich heute die Augen öffne, so erblicke ich dich und sehe meinen Traum erfüllt.
sentences.l: Among the images that passed before my soul was also the comforting one, that a young man came and freed me; and when today I open my eyes, I catch sight of you and see my dream fulfilled.
sentences.i: Among the images that passed before my soul was one of comfort — that a young man came and set me free; and when today I open my eyes, I behold you and see my dream fulfilled.
sentences.n: “an meiner Seele vorübergehen” = to pass before one’s soul (in dream); “vorübergiengen” = vorübergingen. “das tröstliche” = the comforting one (adjective as noun). “dich” = you.

sentences.t: Hilf mir vollbringen was in jenem Gesichte noch weiter geschah.
sentences.l: Help me accomplish what happened further in that vision.
sentences.i: Help me carry out what happened next in that vision.
sentences.n: “vollbringen” = to accomplish, carry out. “Gesicht” here in the old sense = a vision (what was seen in the dream), not “face”; “jenem” = that. “mir” = me (dative).

sentences.t: Das erste ist daß wir den Glaskasten, in welchem mein Schloß sich befindet, auf jenen breiten Stein heben.“
sentences.l: The first thing is that we lift the glass case, in which my castle stands, onto that broad stone.”
sentences.i: The first thing is that we lift the glass case in which my castle stands onto that broad stone.”
sentences.n: “sich befinden” = to be (situated). “heben auf” = to lift onto; “jenen” = that (yonder). Here the maiden’s long speech, begun back at the glass coffin, finally closes.

sentences.t: Der Stein, sobald er beschwert war, hob sich mit dem Fräulein und dem Jüngling in die Höhe, und stieg durch die Öffnung der Decke in den obern Saal, wo sie dann leicht ins Freie gelangen konnten.
sentences.l: The stone, as soon as it was weighted, raised itself with the young lady and the youth on high, and rose through the opening of the ceiling into the upper hall, where they could then easily reach the open air.
sentences.i: As soon as it was weighted, the stone rose up with the young lady and the youth and passed through the opening in the ceiling into the upper hall, from where they could then easily reach the open air.
sentences.n: “beschweren” = to weight, load; “sich in die Höhe heben” = to rise up. “Fräulein” = young lady, unmarried noblewoman; “ins Freie gelangen” = to reach the open; “obern” = oberen.

sentences.t: Hier öffnete das Fräulein den Deckel, und es war wunderbar anzusehen, wie Schloß, Häuser und Gehöfte sich ausdehnten und in größter Schnelligkeit zu natürlicher Größe heranwuchsen.
sentences.l: Here the young lady opened the lid, and it was wonderful to behold how castle, houses and farmsteads spread themselves out and, with the greatest speed, grew up to their natural size.
sentences.i: Here the young lady opened the lid, and it was wonderful to see how castle, houses and farmsteads spread out and, with the greatest speed, grew to their natural size.
sentences.n: “wunderbar anzusehen” = wonderful to behold. “sich ausdehnen” = to expand, spread out; “heranwachsen zu” = to grow up to; “Gehöfte” = farmsteads, homesteads.

sentences.t: Sie kehrten darauf in die unterirdische Höhle zurück und ließen die mit Rauch gefüllten Gläser von dem Steine herauftragen.
sentences.l: They then returned into the underground cave and had the glasses filled with smoke carried up from the stone.
sentences.i: They then went back into the underground cave and had the smoke-filled glasses carried up from the stone.
sentences.n: “zurückkehren” = to return. “die mit Rauch gefüllten Gläser” — attributive phrase, “the glasses filled with smoke.” “herauftragen” = to carry up; “von dem Steine” has the old dative -e.

sentences.t: Kaum hatte das Fräulein die Flaschen geöffnet, so drang der blaue Rauch heraus und verwandelte sich in lebendige Menschen, in welchen das Fräulein ihre Diener und Leute erkannte.
sentences.l: Scarcely had the young lady opened the bottles when the blue smoke pressed out and changed itself into living people, in whom the young lady recognised her servants and folk.
sentences.i: The young lady had scarcely opened the bottles when the blue smoke poured out and turned into living people, in whom she recognised her servants and household.
sentences.n: “kaum … so” = scarcely … when, with verb-first “hatte.” “herausdringen” = to press, pour out; “sich verwandeln in” = to turn into; “Leute” = folk, people (here her household).

sentences.t: Ihre Freude ward noch vermehrt als ihr Bruder, der den Zauberer in dem Stier getödtet hatte, in menschlicher Gestalt aus dem Walde heran kam, und noch denselben Tag reichte das Fräulein, ihrem Versprechen gemäß, dem glücklichen Schneider die Hand am Altare.
sentences.l: Her joy was increased still more when her brother, who had killed the sorcerer in the bull, came up out of the wood in human form; and that very same day the young lady, in keeping with her promise, gave the happy tailor her hand at the altar.
sentences.i: Her joy was heightened still more when her brother, who had killed the sorcerer in the shape of the bull, came up out of the wood in human form; and that very same day the young lady, true to her promise, gave the happy tailor her hand at the altar.
sentences.n: “ward vermehrt” = wurde vermehrt, was increased. “den Zauberer in dem Stier getödtet” — the brother, enchanted as the stag, had killed the sorcerer who fought as the bull. “am Altare” = at the altar (old dative -e — ordinary High German here, though a shared entry marks the form dialectal); “die Hand reichen” = to give one’s hand (in marriage); “ihrem Versprechen gemäß” = in accordance with her promise. “getödtet” = getötet.

glossary.altare: der Altar — altar (dat. sg. with archaic -e; am Altare = at the altar — plain High German here, not Low German)
glossary.band: das Band — ribbon, band (neut.; ein Band stirred by the breath at her breast)
glossary.besinnen: sich besinnen — to reflect, collect oneself (plain High German here, not the dialect sense)
glossary.bestanden: bestehen — to consist (3rd pl. past; bestehen aus = to consist of)
glossary.folge: die Folge — compliance; Folge leisten = to comply with, obey (+ dat.)
glossary.gebrochen: brechen — to break (past part.; den Fuß gebrochen = had broken its leg)
glossary.glase: das Glas — glass (dat. sg. with archaic -e; von … Glase — plain High German here, not Low German)
glossary.lauten: laut — loud (adj., dat.; von einem lauten Lärm = by a loud noise — NOT the verb lauten)
glossary.scheine: der Schein — gleam, light (dat. sg. with old -e; bei dem Scheine = by the gleam)
glossary.sitz: sitzen — sit (imperative; sitz nieder = sit down — NOT aufsitzen/mount)
glossary.sprüngen: der Sprung — leap (dat. pl.; in vollen Sprüngen = at full leap — a High German noun, not the Low German verb)
glossary.wenden: wenden — to turn; sich wenden = to turn (oneself), turn to
glossary.wohlgefallen: das Wohlgefallen — pleasure, liking (Wohlgefallen an etwas haben = to take a liking to)
glossary.worauf: worauf — whereupon, on which (worauf der Stier sank = whereupon the bull sank)
